children: The Indian rupee opened with marginal gains against the US dollar on September 25. The rupee opened 6 paise higher at 95.90 per dollar, compared with Thursday’s close of 95.96.
According to Finrex, Indian Rupee to open around 95.96 almost flat and stay in the range of 95.75 to 96.25 with oil prices continue to remain at near to $ 106 per barrel and dollar index at 101.27.
RBI may continue to be present at < 96.00 keeping rupee in a narrow range as we watch the dollar index march higher while US 10-year moves up to 5.1930%.

Exporters may continue to sell at 95.96 levels keeping the view that RBI may bring the pair down from this level not allowing a movement above 96.00 while importers as usual may continue to buy dips for all cash and near term positions, it added.
Asian currencies traded mixed against the US dollar. The Indonesian Rupiah weakened 0.55%, while the Taiwan Dollar declined 0.33% and the Chinese Renminbi slipped 0.03%.

On the other hand, the South Korean Won gained 0.49%, followed by the Malaysian Ringgit, Thai Baht and Japanese Yen, which advanced 0.39%, 0.19% and 0.13%, respectively. The Philippines Peso and Singapore Dollar were largely steady, rising 0.07% and 0.03%, respectively.

The dollar was set for its first back-to-back weekly gains in more than three months on Friday, as surging Treasury yields and mounting bets on further Federal Reserve rate hikes kept the greenback near multi-month peaks.

Dollar strength pushed the euro to a two-month low of $1.1370 and put it on track for a third weekly decline, its worst losing streak since the end of 2025. Sterling languished near a three-month low of $1.3220 and was on track for its worst weekly performance in four months.

title: Currency Check: Rupee opens marginally higher at 95.90
